Buckhorn Road was impassable from 1 mile east of Moose Ridge Road to Forest Road 129.
Heavy rain produced multiple mudslides on and near Highway 126.  The roadway was closed until the debris could be cleared.
Intense thunderstorm winds destroyed some irrigation equipment.

Intense straight-line winds uprooted two trees.  In addition, a nearby corn field was also flattened west of the location.

A tornado touched down in an open field just southeast of Otis and continued to move east-southeast throughout eastern Washington County. As it approached County Road ZZ it lifted a garage off its foundation anchoring, and shifted it.  The garage door also imploded and about 10% of roof structure was lost. Other damage included snapped trees and broken wood power poles, with lesser damage to outbuildings. The tornado continued to track east-southeast into Yuma County.
Very strong winds flipped a small barn on its side and caused minor shingle damage to a manufactured home.

Hail caused extensive leaf damage to an apple tree and garden.

Minor flooding was observed around roadways in the vicinity to due to heavy rainfall.

Tornado touched down just west of CR 59, along CR 56, moving towards the east-southeast. The tornado impacted one residence after initial touchdown uprooting and snapping several trees on the west side of the property. A few pieces of hard blue plastic window well covering was found embedded into the west facing stucco-ed wall of the home. The tornado then proceeded to impact another residence about one-quarter mile east-southeast where it removed the west facing awning, anchored to the primary houses' roof structure, the northwest facing cement board house siding, and approximately one square of asphalt roofing shingles. The most significant impact was to three telephone poles on CR 59, about one-tenth of a mile south of the CR 56, that were snapped at their bases, resulting in EF-2 damage. The tornado remained on the ground for a few more minutes moving primarily towards the east where it overturned a few center pivot and damaging a working farm's outbuilding. The tornado then lifted over open fields. It was reported, by a trained spotter, that the tornado briefly touched down once more just east of the Caliche School before dissipating. No additional damage was reported.

Travel became very difficult to impossible when heavy snow returned on the 8th. After the lull in snowfall on the 7th, an additional 12 to 24 inches of snow fell late on the 7th through the 9th. This brought total snowfall amounts to 20 to 36 inches, with the heaviest snowfall occurring over eastern Arapahoe County where 31.0 inches of snow fell 6.1 miles SW of Deer Trail. At 5 miles ENE of Byers storm total snowfall of 22 inches was reported.

Snowfall amounts ranged from 5 inches across northern parts of the county to up to 12 inches over southern Washington County through the morning of November 7th. Due to the snow and blowing snow roads across southern Washington County were closed including Highway 36. Here are a few reports, Woodrow 16.8 miles SSE 11.6 inches, Anton 5.8 miles SE 10.0 inches, and Otis 5.7 W 5.5 inches. These snowfall reports are through 7AM November 7th. Snow then subsided for 12-18 before returning. Additional snowfall occurred on the 7th through the 9th was even heavier with additional snowfall of 16 to 24 inches across southern Washington County. For the entire 5 day event, an estimated 24 to 36 inches of snow fell across southern Washington County. At Woodrow 16.8 SSE 26.4 inches of snow was reported and at Anton 5.8 SE 30.0 inches of snow was reported. In addition to the snow, wind gusts of 30 to 40 mph on the 8th produced considerable blowing and drifting snow. Most roads across southern Washington County were closed for an extended time. If not closed, travel was very difficult to impossible due to the very heavy snowfall.

Lasted about 90 seconds. Damage to the roof (was removed) of a commercial building.

Strong microburst hit Denver International Airport in a rare early morning event. Damage occurred to a Delta Airlines plane parked at the airport. The strong winds knocked the plane out of the chocks, and rotated it 90 degrees. Damage occurred to the nose cone as it hit another object, and the aircraft will be out of service. Information was relayed to us by Dave Cunningham, Director of Operations at DIA. He initially had inquired about the winds at the KDEN ASOS, with a brief but high wind gust of 70 mph (61 kts) reported at 410 AM MDT. Four other wind shear sensors on the airport grounds reported gusts in the 50-58 kt range.

Quick moving and rain wrapped tornado swept through Elk Horn Ranch in extreme northern Elbert County before moving into Arapahoe County and lifting. Numerous homes were damaged.
Tornado touched down off of Manila Road in the Arapahoe County side of Bennet, CO and quickly moved north-northeast before lifting. Several properties were damaged.

Larger tornado touched down just south of I-70, captured as a dusty cone tornado on a CDOT web camera, before entering into Bennett in Adams County Colorado where it produced EF2 damage to numerous properties. The tornado made a jog to the east and then lifted just north of 38th Ave.

The largest of the 4 tornadoes on May 18th touched down near 48th and Highway 79 and moved north-northeast over the next 10-minutes. The largest swath of damage occurred just east of Provost Rd where a large barn/workshop was completely destroyed. The tornado then jogged eastward and then looped by to the north where it lifted.

The formation of this tornado was captured well by storm chaser video. The tornado did not have a coherent damage path. There was sporadic damage south of the South Platte River, primarily to a trio of grain silos. Two silos had their tops removed, one was shifted off the pad, another was destroyed. One off duty NWS employee confirmed the location of the tornado as it crossed Logan County Road R just south of County Road 59. The tornado dissipated just southwest of the Prewitt Reservoir with no evidence it crossed I-76.

Well documented tornado that moved south parallel to CO-63, remaining generally in open areas 2-3 miles west of CO-63. We obtained the width (400 yds) of the tornado based on power poles snapped along County Road 50. One single family residence was struck with minor damage to the house, and significant damage to all outbuildings and trees on the property, consistent with EF-1 damage. Debris from the property was carried approximately one mile to the south-southwest. Further south of the damaged property, power poles were snapped and thrown a considerable distance (25 yds), consistent with EF-2 intensity. The power poles were on the west side of AA, just north of County Road 48. Video evidence and the results of the storm survey, suggest that the tornado dissipated just before 6 PM MDT.

Pencil-thin tornado touched down in southern Weld County then slowly moved south across the county line into Morgan County. Several reports of the tornado were received from the fire department and storm chasers/spotter, and it was hard to discern ground contact through the entire path though one funnel was observed throughout the event. The tornado struck an old garage on a farm property just east of County Road 15 in extreme northern Morgan County. The tornado lifted the roof off the garage, which caused the walls to collapse. No other structures on the property were damaged. The owner was on-site during the tornado and mentioned how narrow the tornado was, and that it lifted not long after hitting the old garage.
A landspout tornado was confirmed by Denver International Airport observer as well as  trained spotter and public sources. Location is approximate.

events.event_narrative: The County Road 169 Fire was reported at approximately 12:15 on February 17th, 2026 near Matheson in Elbert County during a red flag weather day. Crews arrived to a wind driven fast moving grass fire in dry conditions near the area of County Rd. 169 and Hwy. 24. The call was upgraded and mutual-aid was requested with evacuations due to the fire moving quickly. A combination of dry cultivated fields and short grass prairie fields provided ample fuel. The added low humidity of only 6% and high winds created a dangerous situation for all personnel. Winds were recorded at more than 70 mph, causing smoke and blowing dust to create visibility hazards. Graders were brought in and a few locals used their own equipment to assist with the firefighting efforts. After more than 5 hours, crews finally contained the fire with an approximate total of 5,598 acres burned.

events.cz_name: N DOUGLAS COUNTY BELOW 6000 FEET / DENVER / W ADAMS & ARAPAHOE COUNTIES / E BROOMFIELD COUNTY

events.event_narrative: Floodwaters up to one foot in depth were reportedly running over U.S. Highway 385. In addition, flash flooding from heavy rains washed out portions of several roads between County Roads 10 and 21.
A small tornado touched and caused minor damage.  Several trees were downed in an open field.  The tornado also damaged a metal fence and minor roof damage to a nearby residence.
A small tornado touched down over open fields.
A tornado damaged several outbuildings and a residence, and downed a number of trees.  In addition, several horses were injured by flying metal debris.

A tornado touched down in southeast Aurora, south of Buckley Airport, and moved south-southeast across open fields, some residential areas, and Southlands Mall.  Numerous homes and apartments suffered window damage, minor roof damage and there were a few broken garage doors.  The Southlands Mall had some roof and window damage, and wall damage to one of its restaurants.  South of the mall, Lowe's received some roof damage, and lightweight sheds and other structures were destroyed.  One resident, in the Sorrel Ranch subdivision, north of the mall, was swept off his porch while attempting to get close-up pictures of the tornado.  He was found unconcious and bleeding in his front yard, with a dislocated shoulder, an injured neck, and multiple other injuries.  In addition, the tornado flipped a trailer home.  A man inside the trailer suffered minor injuries.
Strong outflow winds from a severe thunderstorm snapped two pine trees, approximately 25 to 30 feet tall, near the base.
Hail, up to 4 inches in depth, covered the roadways.
A tornado touched down but did no damage.
A tornado touched down but did no damage.
A tornado touched down but did no damage.

Heavy rain from numerous thunderstorms produced extensive flooding of roads and ditches along the Wildcat Creek area.  One resident measured 5 1/2 inches of rainfall with the storms.  Law enforcement reported State Highway 52 and County Road AA were under several feet of water.  Several other county roads were damaged by heavy rain with extensive field flooding reported.  One accident occurred when a driver drove his truck into the washed out portion of County Road Y just east of State Highway 52.  He escaped the submerged truck uninjured.
A tornado touched down but did no damage.

The tornado began 8 miles south-southwest of Elizabeth and produced minor damage to two homes.  The tornado then moved southeast and intensified with EF1 and EF2 damage observed 9 miles south of Elizabeth, with substantial damage to a farm, trees, and snapped power poles.   The tornado moved on a more southerly track for the next 2 miles with additional EF1 and EF2 damage 11 miles south of Elizabeth.  The tornado leveled a 70-yr old barn and a nearby cinder-block shed was torn open.  Major tree damage was also observed.   The tornado then continued southward for another mile before lifting with some EF0 and EF1 damage 12 miles south of Elizabeth.  Minor damage to another home was observed with several large trees uprooted.
A small tornado touched down.  An airplane hanger was damaged and small plane flipped.
A tornado touched down but did no damage.

A severe thunderstorm caused extensive damage to wheat and corn crops in the immediate area.  Out of 104,000 planted acres of wheat in Phillips County; 3,000 were destroyed.  Sixty thousand additional acres were damaged.  Out of 102,000 planted acres of corn in the county; 2,000 were completely destroyed and 20,500 were damaged.
A man was killed by lightning while crossing an open field.  The victim was struck behind the right ear; the bolt then exited out both of his ankles.

A 41-yr old man was injured when he was struck by lightning on a golf course in Greeley. He was was struck on the 13th hole and suffered burns to his body, but was alert and concious when paramedics arrived.
A small tornado touched down but did no damage.
A small tornado touched down and damaged a picnic table at a Douglas County Sheriff training facility.
A small tornado touched down but did no damage.
A small tornado touched down but did no damage.
A small tornado touched down but did no damage.
A tornado touched down but did no damage.
Strong winds downed branches two to three inches in diameter.
A strong thunderstorm wind gust blew a luggage car into a Southwest Airline airplane causing some damage.
A tornado touched down but did no damage.
Thunderstorm winds downed tree branches 10 inches in diameter.
Two large trees were blown down onto the intersection of County Roads 18 and 19.

Damaging thunderstorm winds toppled two grain elevators and knocked a tree into a home.  In addition, some empty trailers were blown onto their sides.  Some outbuildings at High Plains Livestock suffered roof damage and broken windows.  The combination of strong wind and marble size hail also caused extensive crop damage.
Large hail caused extensive damage to a wheat field.
Strong thunderstorm winds downed numerous tree branches.

Thunderstorm winds downed numerous trees and caused extensive crop damage.  Most of the corn stalks in the vicinity of Fort Morgan were snapped at the base.  The wind ripped the doors off several feed sheds and other small buildings.  Power lines were also downed which caused scattered electrical outages.
A wet microburst produced strong winds and very heavy rain; 1.5 inches in 30 minutes.
A tornado touched down briefly but did  no damage.
Microburst winds downed a light pole in Sterling, along with several trees.  A roof was also torn off an apartment building.
Damaging winds from a wet microburst downed two 30-ft flag poles.  Several tree branches 3 inches in diameter were snapped, and a wind gage broke.

events.event_narrative: A small tornado touched down and crossed Interstate 70, flipping a semi-trailer.
Lightning struck and apartment complex, knocking some bricks from a building in the complex.  A water heater was also damaged.
Lightning struck a veterinary hospital, damaging an exterior electrical box.
Thunderstorm winds knocked a tree on to two vehicles in Boulder.  One of the two drivers was injured when the tree smashed the windshield of her car.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding near Livermore, which produced major street flooding.  Several basements were flooded in Wellington.  Automated rain guages recorded 3.35 inches of rain in the town of Laporte.

A very short but intense wet microburst produced damaging winds.  Numerous tree limbs and some trees were downed around Fort Morgan and Brush.  Downed power lines ignited at least two utility pole fires and caused scattered electrical outages.

A wet microburst contributed to a fatal car accident near Holyoke.  The combination of very strong winds and heavy rain caused extremely poor visibilities.  The severe thunderstorms wind rolled a semi truck hauling an empty trailer on its side.  The trailer came to rest on the center median while the truck ended up in the left eastbound lane.   A van following behind then struck the undercarriage of the rolled over semi truck and ran off the road.  The driver the of the van was killed.  His teenage son and the driver of the truck suffered minor injuries.
Thunderstorm outflow winds snapped a large tree branch which damaged two parked vehicles at Colorado State University's Oval.
Large hail broke a skylight.
A tornado touched down but did no damage.
Strong thunderstorm winds snapped tree branches two inches in diameter.
Intense thunderstorm winds destroyed a small shed.
A tornado touched down but did no damage.
A small tornado touched down but did no damage.
A small tornado touched down but did no damage.

Flash Flooding occurred when torrential rain and hail caused a nearby creek to jump its banks.  The creek inundated State Highway 71 with 3 feet of water.  Several county roads in the immediate vicinity were also washed out and closed until they could be repaired.
Several power poles were completely removed from the ground, knocking out electrical power when a tornado touched down. Some trees and a home were also damaged.
Lightning struck the Darlington Prismatic Electric Fountain in City Park's Lake.
Intense thunderstorm winds knocked two power poles down at the intersection of County Roads 33 and 98.
Large hail caused minor damage to a vehicle.
Heavy rain caused several mudslides along State Highway 67 near Oxyoke, north of Deckers.  Five washout areas were observed.
Heavy rain triggered a mudslide along State Highway 126 at 6-Mile Hill.

A wet microburst produced damaging wind and very heavy rain in the Fort Morgan area.  Flash flooding occurred in Fort Morgan when up to 2 inches of rain reportedly fell in less than 20 minutes.  Some parts of the city were inundated with 2.5 feet of standing water.  Along County Road 20, up to 3 feet of water covered parts of the roadway.  Minor flooding was also reported in Log Lane Village.
Heavy rain caused significant trail damage in Castlewood Canyon.  A couple of wooden walkways over the creek were also washed out.

Intense thunderstorm winds destroyed an outbuilding and a pivot sprinkler on a farm.  A semi-trailer traveling along Interstate 76 was also blown on its side.  The driver was uninjured although the damage to his truck was extensive.

Six children received minor injuries when lightning struck a nearby tree.  The injuries occurred when they were knocked down by the blast.  None of the children suffered burns or appeared to have been directly hit by the lightning.

Two separate storms moved across Miller Farm, near State Highway 66 and County Road 19, and caused widespread crop damage.  Approximately 200 acres of the farm was devastated by strong winds, heavy rain and hail.  In all, 400 farms were directly impacted by the storms with widespread crop damage across Larimer and Weld Counties.

Heavy rain produced mudslides in the Hayman burn area.  Trees, stumps, sticks,  debris, and decomposed granite came down with the mudslides.   Most of the damage occurred from Six Mile Creek to Forest Service Road 211 above the Wigwam Fishing Club.   Road crews had to totally restore shoulders and slopes and cleaned out ditches downstream of draws and ravines.  The mudslides washed out a 250-ft stretch of one shoulder of State Highway 126, near the turnoff to Cheesman Reservoir, and a large section of guard rail was washed out.

Heavy rain, mud and debris came down onto State Highway 67, about 5 miles south of Deckers, completely closing the highway.  Due to the amount of debris, the creek was rerouted onto the highway, damaging the road.  Storm totals up to 1.75 inches were reported.  Several motorists were reportedly stranded in the area and had to be rescued.
Straightline winds from a wet microburst overturned a van trailer and tore the roof off a shed.  Several large tree branches were also snapped.
Intense outflow winds associated with a severe thunderstorm damaged a barn.
Major flooding was observed in Crook.  Anywhere from 1 to 3 feet of standing water was reported in parts of town.

Intense thunderstorm winds downed several power lines.  At least 1,200 homes were without power in parts of Sterling and Atwood.  The wind also wreaked havoc at the fairgrounds where tents and awnings covering booths were blown off.
A small tornado touched down but did no damage.

Large hail, up to grapefruit size, damaged corn crops.  Most of the crop damage occurred north of State Highway 34 to Morgan County U, and along State Highway 144, east of State Highway 39.  Damage to homes and vehicles was also reported.  Minor damage was also reported at the Fort Morgan Golf Course.

Large hail broke out skylights in several recreational vehicles at an RV and trailer park in Greeley.  Vehicles in several car dealerships in Greeley were damaged as well.  The combination of heavy rain and hail also caused extensive street flooding.  City Hall in Greeley reported minor flooding.  Several basements were also flooded.
Several windows were broken and some poultry killed.
Crop damage was reported in the immediate vicinity.
Some farm equipment and fiberglass structures were damaged by hail.
A small tornado touched down but did no damage.

North of Eleven Mile State Park, the tornado destroyed to small sheds and a camper, while a steel framed barn suffered major damage.  Two homes received minor damage including:  broken windows, cracked siding, lost shingles and a collapsed deck awning.  At another property northeast of Lake George, another camper was flipped and destroyed.  Minor damage was also observed with signs knocked down along State Highway 24.  Between Eleven Mile Reservoir and Lake George, there were numerous areas of significant tree damage.  Large ponderosa pines, two feet in diameter, were uprooted and snapped off.

A woman riding her bike in training for an Ironman Triathalon was struck by lightning.  She was in the 78th mile of a 100-mile training ride when she was hit.  Initially, she lost her vision and couldn't move her arms.  After a short stay in the hospital, she made a full recovery.
Lightning struck a very large tree in southwest Denver.  The tree fell on fences and knocked down power lines.
Lightning ignited two oil tanks near Bennett.  It took 18,000 gallons of water and foam to put out the fires.
Lightning struck and killed a 2-yr old horse at Colorado Horse Rescue's Longmont farm.
Lightning sparked a fire which charred approximately 1000 acres of wheat stubble.
Lightning ignited an oil tank approximately 12-ft in diameter and 25-ft high.

events.event_narrative: The combination of very heavy rain and large hail produced flash flooding along State Highway 52 near Hudson and Keenseburg.  Up to 18 inches of water flowed across sections of the highway, damaging the roadway.  The most severe damage was reported at the intersection of State Highway 52 and County Road 49.  Extensive crop damage was also reported in the area.  The highway remained closed until the floodwaters subsided.

Intense thunderstorm winds caused extensive damage to the exterior of a garage shop along with scores of livestock shelters.

Heavy rain and torrential hail produced flash flooding over southeast Weld County.  Fifty thousand acres of cropland was heavily damaged.  Ham radio spotters reported water running across State Highway 52, east of Prospect Valley, forcing its closure.  In addition, State Highways 14 and 392 near Briggdale were also inundated with water.  Several county roads were either flooded or completely washed out.
Heavy rain either flooded or washed out several county roads including 51 and 82.

Heavy rain triggered flash flooding in the Fort Morgan and Brush areas.  Numerous streets were closed due to the high floodwaters.  Flooding was also reported on County Road T, near State Highway 52.  A trained spotter in Fort Morgan measured 3 inches of rainfall.

Severe thunderstorms with large hail and heavy rain produced widespread street flooding in the Fort Morgan and Brush areas.  Several street closures were reported.  Floodwaters were observed across State Highway 71 and Highway R, between County Roads 26 and 27.  Extensive field flooding was also reported around Weldona.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding over parts of County Road 3J, forcing its closure.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding along Interstate 70 at the River Bend Exit.  Several cars were reportedly stuck in the floodwaters.
Heavy rain washed out sections of 20 country roads in Phillips County.
Strong winds from a dry microburst downed several trees in the vicinity of 14th and Federal, and near Bayaud St. and Clarkson St., in Denver.
An intense microburst destroyed a mobile home near Fort Morgan.
Damaging thunderstorm winds snapped tree branches, 6 inches in diameter and larger.  In addition, a roof to a structure under construction was damaged in Iliff and the material tossed.
A tornado touched down in an open field briefly but did no damage.
Intense thunderstorm winds blow a few 50 lb. hay bales 80 to 100 feet.
Intense thunderstorm winds knocked a row of power lines down.  In addition, an estimated 500 lb deck was lifted approximately 15 to 20 ft. off its platform.
Strong microburst winds snapped numerous tree branches, up to 4 inches in diameter.
Heavy rain, up to 2 inches, produced minor flooding in Karval.

Heavy rain washed out a section of County Roads 126 and 128 near Caribou.  Several large boulders were reported across the road.  Considerable flooding was observed in Nederland with some overflows into streets.  Water was reportedly running across County Road 130 between Eldora and Nederland.  Torrential hail, piled up to 8 inches deep, occurred near Eldora.  Several cars were stuck in the ice and the roads had to be closed temporarily until snowplows could clear the roadways.
Damaging microburst winds uprooted some trees.
Intense winds associated with a microburst downed power lines.
A strong thunderstorm produced heavy rain and caused minor street flooding.

Intense thunderstorms, producing heavy rainfall in excess of 5 inches in one hour, produced flash flooding in the vicinity of Elizabeth.  Numerous county roads were washed out.  The combination of heavy rain and hail made it necessary to run snow plows through the town.  Extensive basement flooding was also observed.

Flash flooding was reported 1 mile north of Loveland and 3 miles south of Masonville.   State Highways 27 and 29 were inundated with up to a foot of water, rocks and mud.  Heavy rain caused 6 to 10 inches of rain to stream across County Road 27.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding near Interstate 70 at Byers.  Two feet of water was observed moving across the exit ramp.  One car was washed into a tree but no one was injured.
Lightning sparked a fire to a home in west Loveland, causing extensive damage to the roof, attic and garage.
County Road 51, between State Highway 392 and County Road 74,was inundated with 6 to 8 inches of water.  A trained spotter measured 2.53 inches of rain near this location.
A tornado touched down briefly in an open field but did no damage.
A tornado touched down and destroyed half of a barn.

A tornado touched down near a home.  It uprooted trees and did some damage to the home, breaking windows some windows.  Two horse trailers were picked up and thrown approximately 100 yards.  Several hundred yards of fence were torn out of the ground, and several wood and steel fence posts were torn out of the ground.  Debris was found up to a mile from where the tornado touched down.  A small horse barn that had been recently built was also destroyed; one horse was badly injured and was later euthanized.
Thunderstorms producing very heavy rain caused flash flooding near Kutch.  Several county roads were washed out by the floodwaters.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in and around Fort Morgan.   Widespread flooding was reported to homes and businesses.  Basements were flooded as the streets were  inundated with 1 to 3 feet of standing water.  Radar estimated up to 3 inches of rain had fallen in the area.

A 14-year-old teenager was struck by lightning while washing her family's car.  The bolt struck the street nearby; it then traveled up a stream of water flowing from the vehicle and hit the teenager.  She received minor injuries.
A lightning strike sparked a small grass fire near Quaker Street and Golden Road.  It was quickly extinguished by emergency responders.
Lightning struck a tree in Morrison.
Lightning sparked a fire in a restaurant shortly after midnight.  It caused extensive damage.

A hiker was struck while traversing The Narrows portion of Longs Peak in Rocky Mountain National Park.  The 31-year-old man was struck late in the afternoon at an elevation of 13,800 ft. after taking shelter under a rock ledge when a storm approached.  The lightning apparently struck a rock then hit the man in the head.   He was knocked out for approximately 14 hours and was not found until the next morning.  The man suffered from numerous burn injuries.  He was concious and able to walk slowly.  He recalled his hair standing on end but was unable to remember being hit by the lightning.
Lightning struck a residence and sparked a fire.  The fire migrated in the space between the first and second floor.
Lightning sparked a fire at a townhome.  The fire caused damage to the exterior roof and severe damage to the trusses in the attic.
Lightning strikes caused minor damage to two businesses.

events.event_narrative: The dry, warm and windy conditions that started the month of April allowed for another large wildfire to develop in the foothills of Larimer County, about 10 miles northwest of Masonville. The fire spread after strong winds allowed a slash pile burn to get out of control. The wildfire consumed 2,940 acres. Hundreds of residents were forced to evacuate their homes due to very strong winds. Thirteen homes were destroyed in addition to numerous vehicles and outbuildings. The total cost of fighting the fire alone was around $3 million.

events.event_narrative: A large avalanche killed five snowboarders over Loveland Pass.
A small tornado touched down but did no damage.
A tornado touched down briefly but did no damage.
A tornado touched down briefly but did no damage.
A severe thunderstorm produced strong winds which downed a power pole.
A tornado touched down briefly but did no damage.
A severe thunderstorm broke tree limbs, breaking limbs up to 3 inches in diameter.
A tornado touched down east of the Denver International Airport Concourses but caused only minor damage.
Strong winds associated with a severe thunderstorm knocked down power lines.
Damaging thunderstorm winds snapped large branches, up to six inches in diameter.
Heavy rain produced debris and mud flows in the High Park burn area.
Lightning struck down and destroyed a large tree in the Colorado State University annual flower trial garden.
Lightning injured a hiker.
Lightning injured nine migrant workers.
Part of a roof was blown off a building.
Damaging thunderstorm winds snapped tree limbs, up to 1.5 inches in diameter.
An intense thunderstorm wind flipped over a semi-trailer in the eastbound lane of Interstate 70.
Intense thunderstorm winds partially peeled aluminum siding and some roofing material off of some storage sheds.  Several trees also suffered minor damage.
Intense thunderstorm winds caused scattered electrical outages.
Numerous power poles were snapped which caused widespread electrical outages in and aound Deer Trail.
An intense thunderstorm wind downed a tree.
Mudslides due to very heavy rain, forced the closure of Highway 14, in the High Park burn area.

Thunderstorms produced very heavy rain in Lincoln County.  Six inches of running water was reported across County Road 2W.  The area of water covered approximately 30 to 45 feet of the roadway.  In addition, 12 inches of water, approximately 100 to 150 feet in width, was observed running across County Roads 33 and 109.

Heavy rain forced the closure of Rist Canyon Road, between Davis Ranch Road and the canyon mouth, in the High Park burn area.  At least a foot of water was observed running across the roadway in several areas.  A significant mudslide was reported on Colorado Highway 14 in Poudre Canyon. At one point, the highway was closed in two spots to clear the debris from the roadway.

Heavy rain washed out approximately 100 to 150 yards of the Fern Lake Trail, stranding a group of horseback riders.   A large debris flow covered the trail about one mile west of the trailhead near a feature called Arch Rocks. The debris flow originated on the slope to the north of the trail in the Fern Lake burn area.  The debris, consisting primarily of mud, rocks and trees, and was estimated to be four feet deep in places.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding along Colorado Highway 61 and Mile Marker 15. All the county roads east of the highway and north of County Road 54 were closed by floodwaters.   Extensive flooding washed out several of the county roads.
A mudslide forced the closure of Colorado Highway 14 in the High Park burn area.
Very large hail caused extensive damage to homes, automobiles and trees and crops.
A tornado touched down briefly in an open field.  No damage was reported.
A tornado touched down briefly in an open field.  No damage was reported.
A tornado touched down briefly in an open field.  No damage was reported.
A tornado touched down briefly.  Some damage was reported.
Thunderstorm winds snapped large tree branches, up to 12 inches in diameter.
A tornado touched down briefly in an open field.  No damage was reported.

A velodrome under construction was heavily damaged by heavy rain and high winds.  The wind toppled the eastern third of the 250-meter cycling track. Bolts measuring one-half-inch thick by 7 1/2 inches in length were ripped out of concrete footers while 16-inch-wide trusses, collapsed under the force of the wind. In town, heavy rain, around 2.5 inches in less than one hour, caused extensive street flooding.  The intense wind also downed trees which resulted in localized power outages. In addition, an empty semi-trailer was blown on its side.
A tornado touched down briefly in an open field.  No damage was reported.
A microburst downed numerous trees and power outages in in east central Denver.
Several trees were blown down.

Running water, up to a depth of 12 inches, and 50 feet wide was running across the intersection of 95th Street and Lookout Road near Niwot.  The floodwaters forced the closure of Erie Parkway.  Later a 4 to 5 ft wall of water, was reportedly observed running  through the area.
Heavy rainfall produced a mudslide at Left Hand and Olde Stage Road.  One foot of debris was reported on the roadway near Gregory Canyon.
Heavy rain producing thunderstorms caused extensive flooding of creeks and fields.  Numerous dirt roads were damaged or washed out completely.

Flash flooding forced numerous road closures in the city of Boulder including Lookout Road, from 79th to 95th, and South Boulder Road near Cherryvale.  In addition, culverts were reportedly overflowing at 51st and Kelso Road.  In Erie, Vista Parkway was inundated with 3 ft of standing water.
Flash flooding forced the closure of Erie Parkway, between Briggs Street and Weld County Road 7.

Flash flooding was observed in the High Park burn area.  It forced the closure of CO14, between Rustic and Teds Place.  Other road closures included Larimer County Road 70 between County Roads 20 and 21.

In Boulder, Old Tale Road at McSorley was closed due to debris and downed trees.  Debris forced the partial closure of 3rd Street and Canyon and the Eastbound lane of Baseline Road near Foothills Parkway.  Flooding was also reported at:  9th and Alpine,   9th and Balsam and South Boulder Road at Manhatten Street.  Two teenagers in Boulder were killed when they abandoned their vehicle while trying to flee the floodwaters.  The two other occupants suffered minor injuries; one escaped the vehicle while the other remained in the car and was later rescued.  In the city of Boulder, 61 properties were destroyed.||In the Fourmile burn area, widespread flash flooding and debris flows forced the closure of Fourmile Canyon at Boulder Canyon.  Water was also reportedly flowing over Gold Run Road at Ingram Gulch due to a blocked culvert.  Major structural damage occurred in Fourmile Canyon and Jamestown, which forced a mandatory evacuation of all residents.  A man in Jamestown was killed when the building he was in collapsed.  In the Jamestown area, 26 properties were destroyed.  Flash flooding was also reported in Lefthand Canyon. In unincorporated Boulder County, a total of 86 properties were destroyed.

Flash flooding and debris was reportedly washed out a sections of CO72 at the base of Coal Creek Canyon.  Road closures included:  CO72 , from CO93 to Coal Creek Canyon; CO93, between CO72 and CO128;  CO72, between CO93 and Indiana St.; U.S. 36, between Wadsworth Blvd and Flatirons;  Interstate 70 west, from Floyd Hill to Hidden Valley due to rock slides.  Natural Gas Lines in Coal Creek Canyon were also shut off.

Heavy rain caused five very small dams in the Big Elk Meadows area to fail.  As a result, a family became trapped when a county road was washed out and floodwaters damaged their home.  Road closures included:  U.S. 34 east/west, between Loveland and Estes Park; CO14 east/west, between Walden and Ted's Place.  Larimer County Roads 27E, 25E, 52E and 54E were all closed near La Porte due to flash flooding.  Several roads were also washed out southwest of Loveland and north of Fort Collins.

In Boulder, many vehicles were abandoned near Lookout Road and Spine due to floodwaters.  Significant flooding was reported at the Justice Center; the Juvenile Detention Center had to be evacuated to the second floor.  Floodwaters to a depth of 2 feet inundated Hawthorne Street in north Boulder.  Moderate flooding was observed along Boulder Creek.  Boulder Canyon was closed due to flash flooding.  Numerous rock and mudslides made Lefthand Canyon impassable. Major structures were lost in Jamestown.  In Lyons, rock and mud slides were also reported and the Waste Water Treatment Plant was breached.  An 80-yr old man was killed when his truck was swept into the St. Vrain River.  He had returned to his home to look for his wife.  His vehicle was found 200 yards from their residence.  In town, 82 properties were destroyed.  Mandatory evacuations were ordered in Longmont, along the Lefthand and St. Vrain Creeks.  In Longmont, 53 properties were destroyed.
Flash flooding in Coal Creek Canyon caused a gas line break which impacted 1500 homes.  The areal coverage of the flooding increased along Coal Creek.
Flash flooding forced the closure of CO36, between Wadsworth Blvd and Flatirons.
Flooding was occurring along Boulder Creek in Boulder where it crested.  Flooding also occurred along South Boulder Creek near Eldorado Springs with flooding impacting nearby homes.

Heavy rain, ranging from 6 to 12 inches through the storm event caused widespread flooding, including the entire drainage systems of the Big Thompson and Cache La Poudre Rivers.  Some of the hardest hit communities included:  Estes Park, Drake, Glen Haven, High Park burn area and Loveland.  Most of the parks, trails and open spaces in Larimer County suffered some degree of damage.  Dams in the Big Elk Meadows area failed which drained into the Little Thompson River.  Multiple structures were reportedly damaged, with several rescues from the flood and infrastructure damage.  Power lines were also downed.  Road closure included U.S. 36, from Estes Park to CO66.  Mandatory evacuations were ordered for residents along the Big Thompson River on the west side of Loveland.  The county experienced issues with water and wastewater plants due to flooding. In Fort Collins, an estimated 20 businesses and 10 homes were damaged by floodwaters.  ||Preliminary damage estimates included $89 million to roads and bridges throughout the county.  In addition, damage to the sewer system in Estes Park could total more than $20 million.  At least 1,700 homes were destroyed in Larimer County, and an estimated 16,300 dwellings were damaged throughout the flood zone.

Heavy rain, ranging from 4 to 10 inches through the entire storm event, caused widespread flooding along entire drainage system of the Cache La Poudre River including Greeley and vicinity. In Evans, thousands of residents were told not to flush their toilets or shower, prompting Greeley-Evans School District 6 to close schools.  Similar problems occurred in Lasalle.  County commissioners  estimated at least $230 million in damages to properties and infrastructure throughout Weld County.  County officials estimated more than 7,000 parcels of land were impacted by floodwaters; 2,900 were residential and 2,300 were agricultural.  In addition, 355 commercial and 62 industrial properties were damaged.  A total of 140 county roads were closed at some point, with 654 lane miles of the county's roadways impacted by the flood.  Sixty-four irrigation canals were also damaged.  As a precaution, about 1,900 oil and gas wells had to be shut down.

Heavy rain, ranging from 4 to 10 inches through the entire storm event, caused widespread flooding along the entire drainage system of the South Platte River.    Flooding and flash flooding inpacted Riverdale Golf Course and the Regional Park. The gulch that ran through those two areas caused flooding and erosion in several places including the newly created reservoirs between the Regional Park and 120th Avenue.|The Regional Park shop was also flooded as well as the Riverdale Golf Shop.  All combined, the county���s estimated damage at the Park alone, not including the golf course, was about $637,000. Parts of Colorado Boulevard between CO7 and 168th Avenue were closed due to significant damage to the road surface and foundation.|Additional damage also occurred at retention ponds, parks and trails.  The cost to roads and bridges was approximately $400,000 for repairs.  Approximately 755 households were impacted by flooding.

Heavy rain, ranging from 4 to 12 inches through the entire storm event, caused widespread flooding along the entire drainage systems of East Tollgate and Coal Creeks. The areas around Parker Road and Piney Creek  were flooded as several holding ponds did overflow their banks.  Some of the worst flooded in Centenniel occurred along Arapahoe Road near Cottonwood.   According to FEMA, 2,138 households were impacted by flooding.||Road closures included:  East Fitzsimons Pkwy. and North Peoria, East 26th Ave and Fulton St., East 17th Ave and Dayton St., East Colfax and Peoria St., East 12th Ave. between Xanthia St. and Xenia St, East 12th Ave. and Yosemite St., East 11th Ave. and Willow St., East 11th Ave. and Xanthia St., East 11th Ave. and Xenia St., Del Mar Pkwy. and North Havana St., East 1st Ave and Moline St., East Alameda Ave. and South Havana St., South Peoria St. just North of East Ford Ave., South bound 225 and East Alameda Ave., East Alameda Ave. and East Alameda Dr., East Florida Ave. and South Galena St.

Heavy rain, ranging from 6 to 16 inches through the storm event, caused widespread flooding and included the entire drainage systems of Bear, Coal, Clear, Leyden, Ralston and Van Bibber Creeks.   In Arvada, Quaker St. near W. 82nd Ave. was closed due to flooding and infrastructure damage.  Evacuations were ordered in the area of 68th Ave. and 82nd Ave., between McIntyre and Alkire Streets.  Flooding washed out sections of W. 82nd Ave, east of CO93.   Flooding was reported near the intersection of W. 92nd Ave. and Indiana St.  A section of South Golden Road was washed out near Lena Gulch.  Golden Gate Canyon was closed between CO93 and Robinson Hill.  Many other roads in northern Jefferson County were inundated by floodwaters.  Evacuations were also orders between Bear Lake Dam and Echo Lake Drive on Upper Bear Creek.||Preliminary damage estimates totaled more than $6 million.  The most significant damage to roadways, homes and commercial buildings occurred in Evergreen, Coal Creek Canyon and Golden Gate Canyon.  County officials said 14 residences were destroyed and 215 damaged. In addition, 27 commercial properties were damaged. Thirty-five minor structures were destroyed and 57 damaged.

Heavy rain, ranging from 6 to 18 inches through the storm event, caused widespread flooding along the entire drainage systems of Boulder and St. Vrain Creeks.  Three vehicles were partially submerged when floodwaters undercut Dillon Road near CO287, between Lafayette and Broomfield.  When the road first collapsed, several people were able to get out of the water quickly, but three were trapped in their vehicles and had to be rescued.  The three drivers were taken to local hospitals for treatment.  Extensive flooding was reported in Longmont and forced several road closures.  Floodwaters tipped over two storage tanks containing sulfuric acid at the Longmont Brewery.  Several shelters were set up for evacuees.  Numerous  bridges, culverts and roads were damaged in eastern Boulder County.  The town of Lyons was completely isolated by floodwaters.  The wastewater treatment plant was destroyed.  There were numerous rock and mud slides in the area.  Mandatory evacuations were ordered for the entire town of Lyons.  Train tracks were washed out near the intersection of the Diagonal and Jay Road in Boulder.  Boulder Canyon was closed from Nederland to Magnolia.  South Boulder Road was closed due to flooding between Cherryvale and 55th.  About 40 buildings on the University of Boulder campus were damaged and 400 students evacuated. ||According to FEMA, 10,588 homes were impacted by flooding.  Preliminary damage assessments for Boulder, Lyons, Longmont, Jamestown, Superior  and unincorporated Boulder County included:  337 homes destroyed; 428 homes with major damage; 3,426 homes with minor damage; 33 commercial buildings with major damage; 54 commercial buildings with minor damage.  The most extensive damage impacted  lakes and rivers; in particular, along and near the St. Vrain River corridor.  ||The breakdown for the damage estimate in Boulder County included:  $132 million for the city of Longmont; $91.2 million in damage to government facilities, roads and bridges in unincorporated Boulder County;  $49 million for the city of Boulder's infrastructure, parks and open space; $25 million for the county's parks, trails and open spaces.

Heavy rain, ranging from 6 to 10 inches through the entire storm event, caused widespread flooding, including the entire drainage system of South Boulder, Big Dry and Walnut Creeks. Due to extensive flooding, the Spruce Meadows section of the Broomfield Trail was closed due to significant collapses of the embankment between the trail and the adjacent irrigation ditch.
A tornado touched down briefly but did no damage.
Heavy rainfall and flash flooding washed out the east bound lane of James Canyon.  Overland Road was also washed out, along the west bound lane of the Peak to Peak Highway near Jamestown.
Continuous heavy rainfall produced flash flooding.  Floodwaters were reportedly breaking through basement windows west of Brighton.

Continuous heavy rainfall produced flash flooding.  Commerce City officials ordered about 400 residents to leave a neighborhood near the Rocky Mountain Arsenal National Wildlife Refuge due to the potential that further retention ponds would breach.   Extensive flooding was reported in Commerce City with flooded basements, homes and roads under anywhere from 1 to 3 feet of standing water.

Continuous heavy rainfall produced flash flooding. County officials also issued flash flood emergencies downstream for Fort Lupton, Dacono, Platteville and other farming areas as debris piled up near bridges.
Continuous heavy rainfall produced flash flooding that inundated much of central Larimer County including the towns of Drake, Estes Park and Glen Haven.
Continuous heavy rainfall produced widespread flash flooding in the Lyons, with life threatening conditions.
Continuous heavy rainfall produced flash flooding.  East Alameda Parkway between South Chambers Road and South Sable Boulevard was completely underwater.
Continuous heavy rainfall produced flash flooding.  Evacuations were ordered for the Fairfax Park neighborhood in Commerce City, with numerous road closures throughout the city.
Continuous heavy rainfall produced flash flooding.  Standing water at Tower Road caused delays for travelers going to and from Denver International Airport.
Continuous heavy rainfall produced flash flooding.
Continuous heavy rainfall produced flash flooding in and around Estes Park.
Continuous moderate to heavy rainfall produced flash flooding.

Continuous heavy rainfall produced flash flooding along sections of U.S. 34, through Big Thompson Canyon, and U.S. 36, between Estes Park and Lyons.  In addition, a small earth dam was reportedly breached at Big Elk Meadows.

Flash flooding continued with several collapsed homes reported near Jamestown.  Major flooding continued on the South St. Vrain River in northern Boulder County.  Moderate to major flooding was reported in the Fourmile burn area west of Boulder. Moderate flooding was reported along Boulder Creek through the city of Boulder and in Lefthand Canyon.
Continuous heavy rainfall produced flash flooding.  Additional road washouts occurred on side streets within Coal Creek Canyon.  CO72 was completely washed out between Plainview and Twin Spruce.
Continuous heavy rainfall produced flash flooding. Numerous road closures were reported including Highway 36 from Estes Park to Lyons.

Continuous heavy rainfall produced flash flooding.  Weld County Roads 18 and 20 were flooded. Roadways running parallel to Interstate 25, near County Road 11, were inundated with 6 to 8 inches of water.  In Frederick, County Road 18 was washed out at Godding Hollow Pkwy.  County Road 7 was washed out between County Road 20.5 and CO119.  Welland Loop Dr. was also washed out between Drake St. and W. Conservation Dr.

Continuous heavy rainfall produced flash flooding.  Rainfall amounts up to this point ranged from 4 to 7 inches over central Boulder County.  People were trapped as several major creeks flooded including:  Coal Creek, Left Hand Canyon, Fourmile Creek and St. Vrain Creek.  People were reportedly trapped on their roofs.
Continuous heavy rainfall produced flash flooding.  The town of Glen Haven, between Estes Park and Drake, was cut off due to water and debris blocking roads in both directions.
Heavy rain continued to produce widespread flash flooding. Non-stop rain caused road closures, washouts and damage throughout the High Park burn area.
Heavy rain continued to produce widespread flash flooding.  Denver Police evacuated Colfax Avenue to 11th Avenue from Verbena Street to Xanthia Street due to high water in the area.

Heavy rain continued to produce widespread flash flooding.  Aurora's Prairie Waters, a water recycling and purification system, was shut down due to flooding.  Four of the facility's 17 wells where water is siphoned from the South Platte River in Brighton were flooded. Prairie Waters provides up to 20 percent of the city's water.
Heavy rain upstream, including the headwaters of the Big Thompson River, its tributaries and Rocky Mountain National Park continued.
Heavy rain continued to produce widespread flash flooding.  County roads were closed near Livermore with water overtopping sections of the roadway.

Heavy rain continued to produce widespread flash flooding.   A 79-yr old Larimer County resident was killed when she was swept away while trying to climb to safety from her home in Cedar Point. In addition, A 61-yr old Cedar Point resident died when her home was swept down the Big Thompson River by the floodwaters.
Heavy rain continued to produce widespread flash flooding along Leyden Creek.  The creek remained near bankfull on the 13th.

Heavy rain continued to produce widespread flash flooding over areas already inundated by floodwaters.  Road closures included:  East Fitzsimons Pkwy. and North Peoria, East 26th Ave and Fulton St., East 17th Ave and Dayton St., East Colfax and Peoria St., East 12th Ave between Xanthia St. and Xenia St., East 12 Ave. and Yosemite St., East 11th Ave. and Willow St., East 11th Ave. and Xanthia St., East 11th Ave. and Xenia St., Del Mar Pkwy. and North Havana St., East 1st Ave. and Moline St., East Alameda Ave. and South Havana St., South Peoria St. just North of East Ford Ave., South Bound 225 and East Alameda Ave., East Alameda Ave. and East Alameda Dr., East Florida Ave. and South Galena St.  In Aurora, a mother and her baby had to be rescued when her car stalled in a flooded street.
Heavy rain continued to produce widespread flash flooding in the High Park burn area and surrounding locations.

Heavy rain continued to produce widespread flash flooding.  Between 19th and Lombardi, the road was impassable as it was inundated with 15 feet of standing water. Water was reportedly flowing  south to north, approximately 40 feet across Arapahoe Road.  Lee Hill was impassable as well.
Continuous heavy rainfall produced flash flooding.

Continuous moderate to heavy rainfall produced flash flooding.  CO72 was closed from CO119 in Gilpin County to CO93 in Jefferson County.  US 6 from Golden to the junction of US 6 and CO119 was closed in both directions due dangerous conditions from falling rocks.
Continuous moderate to heavy rainfall produced flash flooding.
Continuous heavy rainfall produced widespread flash flooding.
Continuous heavy rainfall produced widespread flash flooding.   The CO36 Turnpike was also submerged by 3 feet of water at Foothills Parkway.
A prolonged period of heavy rain produced widespread flooding.
The combination of heavy rain, coupled with extremely saturated ground conditions, produced additional flash flooding.
The combination of heavy rain, coupled with extremely saturated ground conditions, produced additional flash flooding.  According to FEMA, 113 households in the county were impacted by flooding.
The combination of heavy rain, coupled with extremely saturated ground conditions, produced additional flash flooding.
The combination of heavy rain, coupled with extremely saturated ground conditions, produced additional flash flooding.

The combination of heavy rain, coupled with extremely saturated ground conditions, produced additional flash flooding.   Several inches of water was reported running through the intersection of Lincoln Ave. and Parker.

The combination of heavy rain, coupled with extremely saturated ground conditions, produced additional flash flooding.  Numerous cars were stalled in several inches of standing water near Interstate 225 and Iliff Ave.  Significant over running of ponds and streams was also observed near Chambers Road and Quincy Ave.||Other road closures included:  26th and Picadilly, a 50-ft stretch East and West Bound had moving water flowing over it; I-225 South Bound Closed at Alameda, I-225 South Bound just north of Mississippi Ave down to 1 1/2 lanes of traffic; Alameda and Sable East Bound; Alameda and Chambers West and North Bound, Florida and Abilene South Bound, Expo and Abilene North and South Bound, Jewell and Abilene North Bound, Potomac and 6th North Bound, Hoffman and Potomac West Bound, 14th and Potomac South Bound, Alameda and Havana, All directions; and the intersection of 6th and Havana.

Torrential rain and hail produced flash flooding in and around Greeley and Windsor.  The storm produced widespread flooding and inundated crops, county roads and city streets.  Numerous roadways were closed due to flood waters.  One woman had to be rescued when she was trapped in her vehicle by 3 ft of rushing water.  Several homes and basements were flooded when nearby ditches overflowed.

A man had to be rescued when his car was trapped in flood waters at the intersection of 6th Ave. and Picadilly Road. events.event_narrative: Coal Creek went over its banks and washed out portions of CO72 at Twin Spruce.  The highway was completely washed out between Plainview and Twin Spruce.  Additional washouts occurred on side streets within Coal Creek Canyon.  Many residents were ordered to remain in their homes (Shelter In Place) until rescue teams could reach them.

Flash flooding forced the closure of the Boulder-Denver Turnpike, from McCaslin Blvd. to the Boulder city limits.  The roadway was inundated by 2 ft of standing water near Superior.  Water was reportedly overtopping all the cross bridges along Table Mesa Blvd, from Lehigh to Broadway.  Baseline and 76th was flooded and impassable.  Flash flooding was observed on Marshall Road, about 4 miles south of Boulder.  Another road was washed out at 4th and Hawthorne.  In Superior, one property was destroyed.

Flash flooding continued to worsen  Many roads in the county were impassable with flowing and standing water.  All major roadways out of Boulder were impacted by floodwaters.  During the event, U.S. 36 was closed from McCaslin Blvd. to Flatiron due to major flooding.  Boulder Canyon was reported to be completely washed out.  Evacuations were ordered for residents at the mouth of Boulder Canyon to Broadway, and Pearl to Marine.  In Boulder Canyon, one mudslide was 400 ft. long and 4 ft. deep making the canyon completely impassable.  Boulder Creek was reportedly completely out of its banks in most areas and moving extremely fast.  Newton Court and an apartment were flooded at 1444 Folsom.  Several cars were inundated up to their doors and the first floors of the apartment complex were flooded.  The 1700 block of Marshall was closed during the morning due to major flooding.  Significant road damage was reported in Boulder Canyon.

Flash flooding washed out large sections of U.S. 34 along the Big Thompson River in Big Thompson Canyon.  Numerous roads and streets in and around Loveland were impassable due to the combination of flooding and flash flooding along the Big Thompson River.

In Erie, Kenosha Rd. between 119th and Lombardi was 15 ft. deep and impassable.  CO52 was closed east of the county line road, as it was washed out at Weld County Road 10-1/2.  Boulder Creek completely flooded the Boulder/Weld County Line and CO52 intersection.  The most extensive flooding occurred where Coal Creek and Boulder Creek merged.

events.event_narrative: Highs winds reduced the visibility to near zero along U.S. 34 near Akron.  Multiple accidents resulted in the closure of the highway.
The extent if the damage was minimal and confined to areas west of Sedgwick which included County Roads 1,3,5,7 and 41.

The preliminary damage assessment included:  $1,510,800 for Residential Property Damage; $4,560,000 for County Bridge Infrastructure: $3,350,000 for County Asphault Infrastructure; and $786,000 for Gravel Road Infrastructure.  Most of the damage to the city was sustained in Riverside Park.  The city estimated a total cost of the flood at $20 million, including damages and expenditures.   Agricultural producers in Morgan County saw little damage from the flood overall.

The flood crest moving down the South Platte River completely submerged the community of Messex and forced the evacuation of the small community for several days.  The railroad tracks, owned by the Burlington Northern Santa Fe Railway on the west side of the river, suffered extensive damage.  In addition, a section of CO63 was also damaged. Several small bridges and county roads were washed out by flooding around Messex including Washington County Roads 59, N and WW.  The entrance and exit ramps of Interstate 76 to Barlow Road were closed due to flooding.  Fiber optic cables were also damaged during the flood.

The flood crest continued down the South Platte River and caused widespread flooding as it made its way into the communities of Merino, Atwood, Sterling, Illiff, Proctor and Crook.  Mandatory evacuations were ordered for those communities threatened by record flooding.  The preliminary damage assessment for Logan County indicated 180 residences were affected, with 15 homes completely destroyed. Another 18 homes suffered major damage while 57 had minor damage. There were also 15 mobile homes with minor damage, and 75 accessory structures or private property with minor damage. In addition, 73 miles of asphalt and dirt roads were compromised. All of the main bridges were compromised; eight state bridges and one county bridge.  The Northeast Colorado Health Department implemented the closing of several facilities in the city of Sterling due to the damage of Sterling's wastewater system.  All retail food, body art, childcare and pool facilities were closed until the system was back up and operating.  The headworks facility for the waste water management system was shut down when it became clear the river would swamp the site.

events.event_narrative: A tornado briefly touched down in open country.  No damage was observed.
A tornado touched down briefly in open country; but no damage was observed.
A tornado touched down briefly and extensively damaged a storage shed.
A small tornado touched down briefly; no damage was reported.
A small tornado touched down briefly; no damage was reported.
An intense thunderstorm wind caused minor tree damage.  A shed also suffered minor damage.
A small tornado touched down briefly; no damage was reported.
A large cone tornado touched down in open country.  No damage was observed.
A tornado touched down briefly.  A roof structure collapsed.  An outbuilding and some fencing was also damaged.  Some tree were snapped at their base.
Large trees toppled near 23rd and Galena.

A tornado touched town near Quebec and 6th Ave and lifted near Mount Nebo Memorial Park. This tornado was a non-supercell tornado. Two outflow boundaries from earlier thunderstorms intersected over eastern Denver and western Aurora. This produced localized convergence and wind shear which likely contributed to the rapid formation of the tornado.

Torrential rainfall, from 2 to 2.5 inches, flooded intersections up to 3 feet of standing water at several intersections including:  6th Ave and Lowell, Broadway and Interstate 25, as well as parts of Speer Blvd along Cherry Creek.

The tornado first touched about 3 miles south of Berthoud, and then tracked to the west/northwest and lifted about 6 miles southwest of Berthoud. The majority of the damage was EF1, with some areas of EF2, and a few small areas of EF3.  At least 25 homes between Longmont and Berthoud were damaged; three of them destroyed.  No injuries were reported as the winds tore apart homes and rolled vehicles.

The tornado contiinued its track into Larimer County.  At least 25 homes between Longmont and Berthoud were damaged; three of them destroyed.  No injuries were reported as the winds tore apart homes and rolled vehicles.

Three people were transported to Denver-area hospitals after a lightning strike 500 feet below the summit of Mt. Bierstadt.  A total of fifteen people were hit by lightning.  Eight adults were were transported from the trailhead, and that three of those were taken to Denver-area hospitals. One of them was in serious condition, the other two had non-life threatening injuries.  A dog was also killed.
Heavy rainfall washed out several county roads.
Several roads in the Brush area were inundated by floodwaters.
Numerous roads in southwest Morgan County were inundated by floodwaters.
Heavy rain continued to produce flooding and flash flooding, inundating numerous roads across east central Morgan County.

Flooding and flash flooding washed out several county roads including:  CR73 from CR112 to CR98;  Freese Road from Colorado 86 to CR112; CR102, from Double Tree Ranch to the top of the Bluff; CR9 between Colorado 86 and CR98; CR106, from Canyon Road to CR13; Maul Road also suffered extensive damage.
Heavy rain coupled with already swollen rivers and streams produced flash flooding.  Numerous county roads were inundated by floodwaters.
The small levee breached at the inlet ditch for North Sterling Reservoir.

Heavy rain caused flooding of businesses along the Saint Vrain River in Lyons, south of Bohn Park.  Several basements in Boulder County were reportedly flooded.  Some flooding was also reported along Coal Creek, upstream of Erie.  Road closures included the westbound lane of Arapahoe Road, between County Line Road and 119th Street.

High water levels prompted the release of water through the Fossil Creek Dam Spillway near Interstate 25, southwest of Ft Collins.  Some road closures included:  CR 23, from CR 50E to CR 52E; CR 43, from CR 51B to just east of Glen Haven; CR 15/CR 6C intersection, from CR15 to CR15A to Berthoud.
Heavy rain produced flooding along already swollen creeks and streams in southwestern Weld County.
Floodwaters damaged Arapahoe County Road 42 at the Kingsburrow Bridge.  Water overtopped the road at several locations.

Flooding resulted in numerous road closures in the vicinities of Barnesville, Briggsdale, Firestone, Frederick, Ft Lupton, Gill, Highland Lake, Keenesburg, Kersey, Mead, New Raymer, Riverside Reservoir near Masters, Roggen, Riverside Reservoir near Masters, and Windsor.
Heavy rain and rising levels of South Turkey Creek washed out many driveways.
Heavy rain produced widespread flooding.  Several county roads were impassable.

The combination of saturating rains in the first part of May, and the May 8th and 9th heavy rain storms, produced more water than the creeks and drainages could handle. Flooding due to rain water started to move east through the county washing over county roads, both dirt and pavement).The southwest and northeast portions of the county were greatly affected and the majority of roads in these areas we impassable by vehicle due to water either running over the roads or water cutting trenches through the road.  County roads throughout Morgan County were inundated by floodwaters.  Some parts of the county received at least 10 inches of rainfall over a two week period.

Numerous roads were impassable across western Logan County due to excessive runoff from Pawnee Creek and the South Platte River.  Road closures included:  CR 113 from the Nebraska line to CO 138; CR 72 from CO 113 to CR 51; CR 51 from CR 72 and CR 74; CR 39 from CR 66 to CR 68; CR 49 from CR 72 to CR 74; CR 20 from CR 9 and CR 11; CR 21 and CR 21.5 at CO 14; and CR 37, one half mile north of CR 52.
Widespread minor to moderate lowland flooding was observed along the Cache La Poudre River.
A prolonged period of minor to moderate lowland flooding occurred along the South Platte River.

Heavy rain produced more flooding north of Sterling.  Evacuations were ordered for Globe Meadows and areas between Globe Street and Pioneer Road due to ditch flooding west of a trailer park.  Many farms in the areas reported flooded basements as well as field and roadway flooding.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Loveland.   The Fountain of Loveland, a local wedding and event venue had its outdoor marriage area flooded due to heavy rain.  The business owner observed the area fill up to 5 ft of water in less than 15 minutes.  Minor flooding occurred at the Sam's Club along Eisenhower Blvd.

Flash flooding washed out a 6-ft diameter culvert at the end of Glennon Rd., south of Elbert County Road 186.  A trained spotter measured 2.22 inches of rainfall in 30 minutes, which produced flash flooding.
Major flooding occurred in the westbound lane of Arapahoe Road near the Colorado E470 bridge.
Flash flooding reported in and around Sedalia.
Flash flooding occurred along U.S. Highway 34.

Heavy rain flooded several rural roads.  Basements were also flooded.  Flooding was reported along Coal and Running Creeks.  Elbert County Road 106 was closed due to high water between Elbert County Roads 5 and 13.

In Aurora, water was reportedly flowing over the roads at East 6th Ave. and South Pacadilly Road.  Additional flooding was reported on South Gun Club Road between East Alameda Ave. and East Exposition Avenue, forcing the closure of the road.

Flooding occurred along Plum Creek and its tributaries.  Four trails in Castle Rock were closed due to flooding. Plum Creek remained above flood stage for approximately 2.5 hours, with moderate flooding along and east of the creek.

Heavy rain caused localized flash flooding in parts of Denver.  In downtown Denver, parked cars had standing water rising midway up the wheels.  Denver fire crews had to rescue motorists from flooded intersections and roads.  In Glendale, two lanes of northbound Colorado Blvd. at Exposition Ave. were closed due to flooding.
A tornado touched down briefly but did no damage.
A tornado touched down for a short time but no damage was observed.
A tornado touched down briefly but did no damage.

A well defined tornado touched down and produced some damage. Near U.S. Highway 24, tree branches 1 to 3 inches diameter were snapped.  The tornado then strengthened to a magnitude EF1 tornado as it tracked south of the highway.  Several hardwood trees were snapped near their trunks.  A fuel tank was thrown and a barn damaged.  In addition, a road sign was flattened at its base.
A tornado with an anticyclonic rotation touched down briefly but did no damage.
A tornado touched down and destroyed a pole barn.
A tornado touched down in open country.  No damage was observed.

A well defined tornado touched down and produced some property damage at a farmstead.  The home, barn and nearby outbuildings sustained damage.  A power pole was also snapped about 5 feet above the ground.
Two tornadoes touched down in close proximity to one another, one of which was anticyclonic.  Both occurred in open country so no damage was observed.
A well defined tornado touched down in open country.  No damage was observed.

The last in a series of well defined tornadoes touched down in open country.  No damage was observed.
Heavy rain, with radar estimates up to 8 inches northwest of Longmont, forced numerous road closures.  The heaviest rainfall occurred from around Lyons eastward along the Little Thompson River Basin.

Both the Cache La Poudre and South Platte Rivers crested over a foot above flood stage.  In Greeley, 6th Avenue was closed due to flooding. The water levels forced the closure of Weld County Road 53.  The waters also flooded some nearby homes and farmland.
Significant flooding was observed along the Larimer/Boulder county line.  Numerous roads were closed due to flash flooding.

Flash flooding forced numerous road closures in and around Milliken and Platteville.  Water, up to 3 ft deep, was observed at Division Rd and State Highway 66.  State Highway 60 and Forest Rd were also closed due to floodwaters.

The combination of heavy rain and snowmelt caused minor flooding in southern Jefferson County.  Road closures included West Platte River Rd from Buffalo Creek, and sections of South West River Rd and West Pine Creek Rd.
River flooding forced the closure of twenty campgrounds.  State Highway 67 near Deckers and Spruce Wood were restricted to local traffic only.

Eleven Mile Canyon was evacuated and closed down for several days due to floodwaters threatening to wash out a popular road.  The flooding was the result of an above average winter snowpack from heavy late season rain and snow events in May.
A thunderstorm with very heavy rain, up to 4 inches, produced flash flooding.  Elbert County Road 178, between ERC 53 and Wolf Creek Drive was impassable to high water.
A levee breach along the South Platte River produced farmland flooding over northeast Morgan County. Morgan County Road 7 was also washed out.

A levee breach, about 100 yards wide along the South Platte River, produced farmland flooding over northwest Washington County.  Floodwaters, 3 to 4 feet deep, washed out the Union Pacific railroad tracks southwest of Messex.  Up to 10 inches of water covered several miles of track.  Approximately 30 trains per day had to be diverted until the tracks could be repaired and inspected.  Washington County Road 58.3 was also washed out.
A home sustained some roof and window damage and an RV was blown on its side.
A tornado touched down in open country.  No damage was observed.
A tornado touched down but no damage was observed.
In addition, a wind gust to 60 mph was observed.
A short lived tornado touched down but no damage was observed.
A weak tornado touched down briefly but no damage was observed.
A semi-trailer was over turned near mile marker 350 along Interstate 70.

Heavy rain quickly flooded several intersections.  Vehicles stalled in the flooded intersections.  Two motorists had to be rescued from the flooded roadways; on at University Blvd and County Line Road and the other, at Univerity Blvd and Dry Creek Rd.  At Centennial Airport, a hangar partially collapsed when 2.20 inches fell in one hour.  At the Denver Broncos training facility in Dove Valley, the storm left the practice fields and parking lot flooded, and the viewing area near the field house damaged by strong winds.  The fields, the team said, received 3.5 inches of rain in an hour during the storm.  As a result, the practice facility was closed to the public the following day due to storm damage.

A tornado touched down and damaged the Devil's Head campground and picnic grounds in Pike National Forest as well as the trail to the Fire Lookout Tower.  Six acres of aspen, spruce and fir trees were knocked down.  The tornado touched down at an elevation of 9,700 feet.
A tornado touched down briefly.  It destroyed an outbuilding and caused minor damage to a nearby home.
Another tornado touched down briefly.  Two two grain silos were destroyed and nearby power lines.

A tornado touched down southwest of Hereford and continued to quickly move north northeast into Wyoming.  Areas of sporadic tornado damage were noted from 8 miles south southwest of Hereford to north of Hereford near the Colorado-Wyoming border.  The damage along the patch ranged from EF-0 to EF-1.

Heavy rain combined with torrential hail, clogged drains and caused flash flooding throughout Greeley.  The intersection near U.S. 34 and U.S. 85 was inundated with up to 3 feet of water.  Firefighters rescued several residents from garden level apartments that had flooded.   Several businesses and buildings suffered flood damage, including Greeley City Hall and an apartment complex in Evans. The Greeley Mall was extensively damaged as water poured into the mall from the roof and debris inundated the main floor.  The Frontier Academy Elementary School was also flooded, with administrators canceling classes the following day.
Windsor-Severance Fire Protection District had multiple reports of lightning strikes, including one that hit near Windsor Middle School and set off the school's fire alarms.

The Cameron Peak wildfire became the largest in state history.  It started in a thick forest with very steep terrain.  In the month of August, the fire had consumed 23,021 acres.

In the month of September, the Cameron Peak wildfire consumed an additional 102,075  acres of forestland.  Very cold temperatures after an early season snow on the 8th settled the fire down temporarily, but then a return to very warm and dry weather, coupled with gusty downslope winds to 50 mph on the 26th, fanned the flames and allowed the Cameron Peak fire to continue its expansion through the end of the month.

A powerful tornado swept north-northwestward across Weld County and into Larimer County, carving a path of destruction, nearly 39 miles in length. The tornado, up to one-mile wide at times, initially touched down northeast of Platteville and finally lifted 6 miles west-northwest of Wellington.  A tornado assessment in the aftermath of the tornado revealed extensive areas of damage. On the enhanced Fujita Scale there were pockets of EF3 damage, mainly near the Missile Silo Park Campground, and to businesses and home in eastern Windsor. ||There was one fatality, and 78 injuries. One man was killed when he tried to escape the trailer park in his motor home.  Preliminary estimates from FEMA indicated 850 homes were damaged, and nearly 300 homes were significantly damaged or destroyed. Privately insured damages totaled $147 million, and the Poudre Valley Rural Electric Associated reported $1 million of damage to electric transmission lines.
A tornado touched down and destroyed 5 buildings near Dacono.  One person was injured.  The tornado overturned a five-wheel trailer and injured the man who was sitting inside.

Heavy rain produced a debris flow that impacted CO-125 near Mile Marker 7.  County Road 21 was also flooded near its confluence.  The debris flow forced the closure of the highway until it could be cleared.  A mud/debris flow in the Cabin Creek drainage partially buried a parked USFS vehicle, and trapped the employee behind a washed-out road. The Forest Service employee was assessing one of the closed forest service roads when the storm hit, he was found safe and uninjured.

A debris flow moved into Black Hollow Gulch and damaged or destroyed several structures including four homes.  Four people in one of the homes perished when their residence washed away in the floodwaters.

Thunderstorms produced very heavy rain in southeast Phillips County.  Local law enforcement reported several roads were flooded southeast of Holyoke.  Rainfall measurements from 4 to 9 inches were reported.  Several houses had water rise up to the front doors.  Significant flash flooding was observed 6 miles east of Holyoke on U.S. Highway 6.  Widespread flooding of roads, ditches, and fields was reported. At least one road crossing Frenchman Creek was impassable.  Frenchman Creek and other streams had significant flooding as well.
Heavy rain produced localized flash flooding in the East Troublesome burn area.  Flooding was reported along Gravel Mountain Road from Kauffman Creek.  County Roads 458 and 482 were also flooded.

Heavy rain washed out a crossing along Miller Fork.  The two washouts cut off all access to several residents on Streamside and Corner Court.   The residents sheltered in place until all repairs could be completed.   The Black Creek culvert under Corner Court was also washed out in The Retreat.

Grand County experienced periods of heavy rainfall during the evening.  The commercial operation at Drowsy Water Ranch was heavily impacted. The Ranch began an evacuation of guests to predetermined safe facilities on the property in accordance with their emergency plans.

events.cz_name: BOULDER & JEFFERSON COUNTIES BELOW 6000 FEET / W BROOMFIELD COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Marshall Fire devastated portions of Marshall, Superior and Louisville.  Strong downslope winds, with gusts up to 100 mph, fanned a grass fire that originated near the town of Marshall and quickly spread east to Superior and Louisville.  The fire was the costliest fire in state history, and residential and business property losses alone were estimated to be slightly over $2 Billion.  In all, 1,094 homes were destroyed and 266 homes were damaged.  In addition, 7 commercial properties were destroyed and 30 others sustained damage.  Tens of thousands fled the fire.  Two people died in the fire, while six others were injured.
